subject: Avenue Networks - Security RFP: control mapping & evidence plan
messages:
From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@avenue.com>
To: camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@avenue.com, procurement@avenue.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0500
Subject: Avenue Networks RFP - security control matrix and next steps

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked Redwood’s latency guarantees and the private deployment options. Attached is our standard RFP control matrix (Avenue_RFP_Control_Matrix.xlsx). For the security chapter we need: a control mapping to SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / SIG where applicable, and short-form evidence for each control (artifact name + owner + preferred delivery mechanism).

Key asks from our InfoSec reviewer:
- Control mapping: indicate how Redwood’s controls map to SOC 2 CC/ISO A.5-A.18 and SIG modules where relevant.
- Evidence: samples (syslog retention policy, SOC 2 report redacted pages, KMS architecture diagram, vulnerability scan summary).
- Hosting: confirm Private (VPC) option meets our data residency and key management requirements; include KMS integration notes.
- Timeline: can you provide a curated evidence bundle within 7 business days?

Can you confirm owner and delivery method (Drive link, SFTP, or secure portal)? We prefer a single zip + index if possible.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Lin
Senior Procurement Manager, Avenue Networks
---
Attachment: Avenue_RFP_Control_Matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 280KB)

From: camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@avenue.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 17:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Avenue Networks RFP - security control matrix and next steps

Sara —

Appreciate the matrix and the clear asks. We can produce a curated evidence bundle within 7 business days. Suggested owners and delivery approach below; please flag any special handling needs for PII or regulated PII.

Proposed plan (high level):
- Control mapping: Kimberley will map each Avenue control row to SOC 2 (common criteria) + ISO 27001 Annex A clauses + SIG modules where relevant.
- Evidence bundle: curated artifacts (redacted SOC 2 report pages, KMS architecture diagram, sample audit log extract, scheduled vulnerability summary) assembled into a single zip with a crosswalk CSV. Delivery via secure Drive link gated by a temporary access token; SFTP available on request.
- Private / KMS note: we will include a short note on Redwood Private deployment architecture and how our KMS integrations (AWS KMS / customer-managed keys in GCP/Azure) satisfy your residency & key control requirements.
- Timeline: deliver mapping doc + index draft by Thu, Dec 3; full artifact bundle by Tue, Dec 8.

Action items assigned:
- Kimberly Park: lead control mapping (SOC2/ISO/SIG) — deliver mapping draft 2026-12-03.
- Priyom Das: collect artifacts and produce evidence index + zip — ETA 2026-12-08.
- Jordan Blake: vet KMS note & private deployment language; check for procurement redlines.
- Camila (me): coordinate and review; submit to Avenue once all owners sign off.

We’ll attach the Redwood evidence index (Redwood_SIG_Evidence_Index.pdf) to the final bundle and include per-artifact sensitivity labels.

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Senior Security & Compliance PM
Redwood Inference

---
Note: internal owners copied for acknowledgment.

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0500
Subject: Control mapping progress and questions for Avenue matrix

Team — quick update from my mapping pass this morning. I started with the Avenue sheet and annotated a few tricky mappings where we need the procurement team to confirm scoping:

1) Data classification & labeling (Avenue row 12): Redwood has product-level classification guidance but enforcement depends on customer-provided tagging in Private. I propose we note: "Control partially in product (classification UI + APIs); customer responsibility for data labeling in Private deployments unless Redwood-managed onboarding is contracted."

2) Third-party vendor risk (Avenue row 37): our SIG mapping points to Vendor Management module; we have vendor questionnaires and annual attestation but do not host a consolidated vendor risk register for every customer. Recommend: provide evidence of our vendor intake process + a redacted vendor risk summary for critical suppliers (attachment: vendor-summary-redacted.pdf).

3) Key management (Avenue row 58): confirm dual-mode KMS for Private: customer-managed keys (BYOK) + Redwood-managed envelope encryption for hosted. Need Jordan to finalize short KMS architecture diagram and the wording on HSM/KMS proof-of-control.

Questions for Avenue (to confirm scope):
- For classification enforcement, do you expect Redwood to enforce labels within customer deployments or accept customer responsibility?
- For vendor proof, is a process + redacted sample sufficient, or do you require full registers?

I’ll push the draft mapping to the Drive folder tonight.

— Kimberly
Director, Security Programs
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: vendor-summary-redacted.pdf (application/pdf, 95KB)

From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:42:00 -0500
Subject: Evidence collection ETA & access method

Kimberly / Camila / Jordan —

I’ve started collecting artifacts listed in the index. Current ETA: initial bundle (redacted SOC 2 pages, KMS diagram draft, sample log extract, vuln-scan summary) by EOD Mon, Dec 7. I recommend we use a two-step delivery: 1) upload the zip to a restricted Drive folder with view-only links for Avenue reviewers; 2) for high-sensitivity items (if Avenue requests console access logs or live telemetry samples) we propose a white-glove SFTP transfer with per-file encryption and an NDA addendum.

Notes on artifacts:
- SOC 2: redacted report (service description + control test summaries) — legal OK for redaction.
- Vulnerability scans: 90-day summary and trend chart.
- Audit logs: sample extracts (anonymized) with retention policy doc.
- KMS: architecture PNG + short paragraph describing BYOK options and HSM usage.

I’ll attach the draft Redwood_SIG_Evidence_Index.pdf to the Drive and add a crosswalk CSV keyed to Avenue_RFP_Control_Matrix.xlsx rows.

— Priyom
Security Ops Lead
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 21:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Avenue Networks RFP - security control matrix and next steps

Camila / team —

Thanks for the quick alignment and the proposed timeline — that works for us. A few clarifications from Avenue Security:
- Classification enforcement: Avenue is OK with customer-responsibility for labels in Private deployments; please state that clearly in the mapping.
- Vendor registers: a process plus redacted vendor summary is fine.
- Delivery: Drive link is preferred for initial review; we may request SFTP for any items marked as 'restricted' in your index.

Two small asks before mapping draft: can you flag any controls where Redwood provides only partial coverage (i.e., depends on customer configuration) so our reviewers can triage risk quickly? Also include a short FAQ entry about retention windows for telemetry/logs in Private vs Hosted.

If you can confirm those points in the draft by Thu, Dec 3, procurement will schedule a 30-min tech-validation call for Fri, Dec 4 (optional) to walk through KMS and log access.

Best —
Sara
Senior Procurement Manager, Avenue Networks
